title: Private release stager and rollback playbook generator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated release stager and runbook generator for Redwood Private upgrades. The tool will assemble staged cohorts, preflight checks, canary gating rules, and a machine-readable rollback playbook from version metadata and migration manifests. Goal: reduce manual runbook creation, surface safe fallbacks, and enable telemetry-driven automatic abort/rollback triggers for private (VPC/on-prem) upgrade runs.
acceptance_criteria: CLI or API can produce a per-version release bundle (manifest + staged cohorts + runbook) from a model/operator release tag within < 60s
Generated runbook includes step-by-step commands, required approvals, and automatic rollback hooks that can be consumed by the upgrade agent
Preflight checks execute against a customer-like sandbox and surface blocking signals (schema drift, DB migration preview failures, node capacity shortfall)
Canary gate can be configured to auto-abort based on telemetry (p95 latency, error-rate, KV cache miss), with documented thresholds
Rollout metadata exposed in Console (per-cohort progress, blocked step reasons) and emits standardized telemetry events to the Upgrade dashboard
Integration tests covering dry-run generation, a simulated canary abort, and scripted rollback against the upgrade simulator pass in CI
implementation_notes: Design a small declarative manifest format (YAML) that describes: version, LTS channel, cohort definitions, migration SQL artifacts, preflight commands, expected invariants
Generator will incorporate: version compatibility matrix, LTS policies, pinned component versions, and 'rollback recipe' templates
Expose a 'preview' mode that runs all preflight checks without mutating state; capture outputs and synthesize a risk score
Integrate with existing Private upgrade agent via a contract: /v1/upgrades/start endpoint which accepts the generated bundle
Wire telemetry hooks to Console's Upgrade dashboard and to existing tracing (otlp) so gates can evaluate p95, error-rate, and custom migration metrics
Provide a 'manual approval' gate that posts to Slack channel and requires an approver to click a link (SAML/SSO-aware) before continuing
Ship initial generator as 'alpha' CLI + a lightweight web preview; rollout to internal customers first before external tenants
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (internal): generate bundles for two non-production clusters and run dry-run preflight (2 weeks)
Stage 1 (canary): run staged release against 3 low-risk customer tenants with manual approval gates and telemetry monitoring (2 weeks)
Stage 2 (gradual): expand cohorts to 20% of private fleet with auto-gating enabled; if any auto-abort occurs, execute rollback playbook (4 weeks)
Stage 3 (ga): enable default runbook generation for all scheduled Private upgrades; include opt-out and custom playbook extensions
migration_strategy: Prefer online, idempotent migrations where possible. When transactional migrations are required, generate a two-phase: preview->apply pattern
All SQL DDL must be run with compatibility guards and scheduled with low-traffic windows
Keep a 'compat shim' loader for older control-plane agents to accept bundles and gracefully reject incompatible fields
For heavy data transforms, include a migration-progress probe and a 'quiesce' step that drains incoming requests to affected shards
risks: Automated playbook might miss tenant-specific customizations; mitigated by an 'extensions' hook and manual review step
Telemetry false positives could trigger unnecessary rollbacks; mitigate with smoothing window and multi-signal confirmation
Edge-case migrations (on-prem air-gapped installs) may lack observability; provide offline checklist and fallback manual commands
Tight coupling between generator and agent API could require coordinated versioning—use clear contract versioning and LTS pins
